newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower as strike thins trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower as strike thins trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower on Sunday as volume fell in response to an outbreak of strikes around the country, traders said.
The trading session ended 15 minutes early when the strike finally spread to the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.30 percent, or 0.63 points, to 208.39 on a low all-share turnover of 57 million shekels against 79 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index lost 0.21 percent to 216.55.

"The market is dead. The trading day ended earlier today because of the strike and activity was low. A few of the banks went on reduced schedules, which had a strong impact on trading," said a trader at Bank Leumi.
The Histadrut labour federation called the nationwide strike on Sunday morning following the arrest of a trade union official for not appearing in court in connection with strikes last week.
Union officials were due to meet tonight to decide whether strikes would continue on Monday.
"We saw also some profit-taking and investors are taking a wait-and-see position. It's difficult to say what the market will do in the near future," the trader added.
"The market made a very nice move over the last two months and investors are a little jittery," said Danni Scharia at Capital Securities.

"Investors are waiting for fresh news. They want to see approval of the budget and an agreement on Hebron," Scharia added. "We are getting closer to the end of the year and nobody knows how the new year will open."

Parliament is expected to vote on the 1997 budget on December 31 or shortly thereafter. Meanwhile, Israeli and Palestinian negotiators were due to meet this evening in another round of talks to complete an accord on Israeli redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which gained 1.5 percent to 154,017 on volume of 4.2 million shekels; Bank Leumi, which gained 1.75 percent to 447 on turnover of 3.0 million shekels; and Koor Industries, which fell 0.75 percent to 28,268 on volume of 2.5 million shekels.
